# Source review of the drain's response to a brane bend

**Scoped verdict. The written G0-v0 controller supplies no repulsive response to a pure incident bend at fixed sleeve geometry and fixed incoming carrier data, in either E2 or E3. The native order-converting throat's orientation-dependent force remains undetermined.**

The original card puts the signed source in the mouth energy, `∫η(k_m h²/2−g s h)`. It puts the sink on a different support, `−Γ₀D_s`, where both orientations remove the same positive number per time. Neither support moves when only the incident scalar varies. The carrier action, sources, interface conditions and density/phase outer data contain no `h`, including through its mixed partner `u_L`. A uniform modulation and an imposed slope therefore leave the carrier equations and data identical. The original carrier solution continues to solve them. Claiming unique continuation across arbitrary steady branches would require the deferred kernel/solvability analysis. Translating the annulus in the scalar field *does* give a passive force. In the existing fixed-source ensemble like signed sources attract. Holding the bare source fixed still permits a change in total conormal through the local Robin term. [G0 §§2–4, 6–10](../../software/em_charge_attribute/g0_closure_card_v0.md) · [Electric coefficients, Appendix B](../../software/em_charge_attribute/puncture_deflection_electric_sign_result.md) · [Uniform bend probe](../../software/em_charge_attribute/reports/one_mouth_electric_bend.md)

For a fixed body, the local sink impulse on it is `F_flux = mΓ₀∫D_s v`. At fixed intake, a joint perturbation gives `δF_flux = mΓ₀∫D_s δv`. Likewise the local carrier power removal changes by `−Γ₀∫D_s δe_c` for `e_c=(ε+P)/ρ`. Both are genuine total variations when the carrier state changes. The finite-rank momentum and power corrections act on the remote return and integrate to cancel their respective global carrier ledgers. A change in power has no specified conjugate in-plane displacement here. E3 transmits carrier across the sleeve and mouth. E2 admits it through the mouth alone and includes passive wall pressure in `F_var`. Both have `F_total=F_var+F_flux` in the stationary limit. Neither interface rotates with an imposed `∇h`. The card requires a separate rate-susceptibility perturbation for sign promotion. [G0 §§6.2–6.3, 8–10 and review note 2](../../software/em_charge_attribute/g0_closure_card_v0.md)

Several effects survive attempts to exclude a physical force. The sink centers reflect in `w`, so simultaneous reflection permits an `s₁s₂` carrier interaction. A term `s∇h` in the in-plane force has allowed parity. Its sign and range require a coupling and a solved state. A normal traction on a tilted material face can project into the plane, but its signed amplitude, transfer to the moving body, receiver reaction and support partition are open. Fixed-face carrier runs can have appreciable counteracting loads. A far-field `1/r` bend alone measures the emitting mouth, and a uniform offset probes normal compliance. The independent receiving observable is the orientation-odd **in-plane force** under opposite imposed gradients on the same draining preparation. A separate conjugate work assumption is needed for the earlier repulsive held-bend coefficient. [Force projection and parity](../../docs/em_phaseC_force_decomposition.md#3-the-four-channel-decomposition-the-honest-bookkeeping) · [Joined receiver, finite cuts](../../software/em_charge_attribute/reports/joined_mouth_normal.md) · [Attachment work](../../software/em_charge_attribute/reports/wall_load_to_bend.md) · [Probe definition](../../docs/native_light_em_and_vortex_throat_interpretation.md#78-the-physical-electric-observable-must-be-stated)

In V3 the total material is conserved and its order changes. S12 leaves the conversion and return forms, boundary data and momentum/energy partners open. O2 supplies the in-plane carried term `j_n V^i` on its stated domain, leaving the native bulk-direction transfer and loading open. S11b allows an active interface response with reservoir and budget on its uniform linear domain. It supplies no signed transfer coefficient to a puncture on a bend. The moving-throat magnetic result is conditional on the static electric ensemble. None closes the physical receiving force or supplies two-body translational inertia for 0PN. [S12 §§1, 5](../../research/pde_ledger_v3/steps/S12_order_source.md) · [O2 §2](../../research/pde_ledger_v3/steps/O2_steady_brane_balance.md) · [S11b](../../research/pde_ledger_v3/steps/S11b_interface_coupling_law.md) · [Moving-throat result](../../software/em_charge_attribute/magnetism_moving_throat_result.md)

- **Force on an inclined interface.** PathA-23 derives the material-frame traction $T_{na}=T_{wa}+(T_{ww}\delta_{ab}-T_{ab})\partial_b u_w+O(|\nabla u_w|^2)$. The background mixed current contains $m\rho v_w v_a+\sigma^Q_{wa}$. This is a real candidate if a stream turns relative to an independently responding receiver. One must vary the stress as well as the basis. Isotropic pressure has zero tangent traction but has a horizontal component on a tilted face in laboratory coordinates. Common rotation gives no intrinsic turning signal. Different slopes sampled across a bounded patch start with curvature, which costs another inverse power of source distance for a smooth distant monopole. The recorded sign and magnitude are open for a draining throat. # Force on a held draining mouth in a weak bend

Take an isotropic stationary mouth, one unscreened parity-odd scalar channel and smooth local response. Use a source-free matching sphere and write the slowly varying incident gradient as **g**. For the reduced scalar with gradient energy κ|∇h|²/2, the spatial momentum current is Π = κ(∇h ⊗ ∇h − I|∇h|²/2). With self gradient −L **n**/(4πκr²), the cross current contracted with the outward normal equals −L **g**/(4πr²) pointwise. The scalar therefore delivers +L **g** to the enclosed contents. Like sources attract if the translating body receives that whole force. This also follows for a passive, local, body-attached source by virtual work. Its field and source energies both vary. [Passive attachment](../../../software/em_charge_attribute/reports/wall_load_to_bend.md)

Measure the isolated tail L and total stationary load −**H** on the translating body under opposite gradients, at common incident offset and preparation. Define B by Δ(−**H**) = B **g** and use the parity-odd responses of mirrored mouths. With **d** pointing from source to target, the leading outward pair force is −BₜLₛ/(4πκd²). Reciprocity for nonzero sources requires B/L common to all mouths, and that condition suffices. Like repulsion requires that common ratio negative. Identical nonzero pair strength for *all ordered radii* requires both |L| and |B| independent of radius on a common charge branch. Equal same-radius products alone allow unequal mixed-radius forces. These deductions require independent measurement of both ends of the response and exclusion of other orientation-odd fields or direct remote loads at the same order.

Across the target boundary, −**H** equals the inward scalar current plus the inward current from other cuts, all independent applied forces, minus the storage rate. Include carried momentum and transmitted stress. Count a receiver attached to the translating body inside its boundary. A separately supported receiver carries its own reaction. Thus a positive L needs a non-scalar or recipient-partition increment more negative than −L **g** for repulsion. An identical scalar force on an enlarged assembly can accompany different loads on its translating part. At rest the holder has zero power. During a small translation, measure its signed work, the change in stored energy, the pressure-inclusive energy currents through the cuts, actuator work and any support work at the corresponding velocities. Subtract the matched background at the same throughput. [Fixed-throughput controller and force assignment](../../../software/em_charge_attribute/g0_closure_card_v0.md#62-momentum-and-energy-sourcesall-six-source-slots-fixed)

An inward mass rate supplies no transverse impulse by itself. For a test with w = ℓh, direct equal-speed inlet and outlet beams along s(\(\hat{\mathbf e}_w\) − cℓ**g**) to linear order, where \(\hat{\mathbf e}_w\) points toward the +w side and c = 1 follows the sheet normal. Each beam has the same positive directed thrust T. The force delivered by the stream to the redirector is inlet minus outlet, or sTℓ(c_out − c_in)**g**. A tilting outlet with a stationary inlet gives +sTℓ**g**, and a tilting inlet with a straightened outlet gives −sTℓ**g**. If both track the tilt equally, the change is zero. These three cuts have identical isolated intake, axial thrust and kinetic current. The load reaches whichever part redirects the stream. Pressures or support forces can change it. For a separately applied normal traction the tangent work on a mouth following the graph vanishes because its translation includes dw = ℓ**g**·d**x**. The frozen model lacks the physical h-to-face map, the sided steering and the joined contact partition needed to select any of these cases. [Native graph and traction](../../../research/pde_ledger_v3/directives/O2_SHARED_PHYSICS.md)

The [independent SymPy check](flux_check.py) ran with `python3 scripts/s11c_guarded_run.py --pool em-bend-force-referee --memory-gib 1 --log-directory _scratch/s11c/em-bend-force-referee-20261118a -- python3 _scratch/em_drain_bend_review/force/flux_check.py`. [Literal output](../../s11c/em-bend-force-referee-20261118a/stdout) · [Guard outcome](../../s11c/em-bend-force-referee-20261118a/outcome.json). No commit.

# Transverse recoil in the rounded-receiver benchmark

**Scoped verdict.** Baseline pressure suffices for the first-order flow-induced force on the intact screen projected onto the mouth-center tangent. With zero outer excess momentum export it also fixes the inner-cut momentum supplied to this ideal receiver. Assigning recoil to a physical throat requires the ownership of the inlet, screen and other momentum paths.

The source prescribes outflow across an inner four-dimensional hemisphere and solves a steady incompressible potential flow in a resting upper half-space. Its reflecting equatorial screen occupies `r≥a`. The Python and Wolfram calculations independently obtain the excess pressure and return to the *flat* screen. They do not solve a bent drain. Extending the benchmark requires an imposed static material graph `w=b(x)`, slip without penetration and a cut joined to that graph. Here `b` is a length. [Python lines 13–51](../../software/em_charge_attribute/rounded_end_bulk_flux.py#L13) · [Independent plane calculation](../../software/em_charge_attribute/rounded_end_bulk_flux.wl#L17) · [Recorded scope and finite-cut loads](../../software/em_charge_attribute/reports/rounded_end_bulk_flux.md)

For upper receiving fluid the outward area vector at the screen is `(∇b,−1)d³x`. Contract with the same mouth-center tangent `T_i=e_i+∂ᵢb(X)e_w` at **every** patch. Impermeability removes the advected normal momentum there. To first order the fluid's excess force **on the screen** is

`F_i = ∫_{r≥a} Δp₀(r)[∂ᵢb(x)−∂ᵢb(X)] d³x`.

The perturbed pressure and variation of the edge's projected location multiply a vanishing flat-screen tangential integrand. A lower receiver reverses the area vector. This subtraction of slopes represents projection on the specified tangent. A fixed lab-horizontal force has a different expression. Subtract the uniform rest pressure on the **same bent geometry** throughout the balance. An uncompensated pressure difference across a real screen is a separate load.

For a finite spherical source of a three-dimensional harmonic bend outside its support, every concentric receiver sphere before the source has mean gradient equal to the mouth gradient. For a decaying Newtonian potential, the mean gradient vanishes on spheres enclosing the entire source, by the spherical-shell identity applied to each source element. The uniform local tilt cancels. For fixed radii and nonzero source monopole, the first-order screen force scales as `d⁻⁵` at large separation from the weighting of the distant screen, since `Δp₀=O(r⁻⁶)` and the center slope is `O(d⁻²)`. For an upper receiver and a positive bend monopole, the leading screen force points toward the distant bend source. The central actuator delivering the inlet momentum has the opposite recoil.

These sign assignments require steady momentum balance, quiescent infinity and sufficiently rapid decay of **excess momentum flux integrated over the outer cut**. The cut is a bookkeeping surface. The pressure return is distributed over the screen. Counting a central inlet actuator and its attached screen together cancels these two exchanges when the far cut carries none. A real second drain can change the receiver flow, add another opening, or carry momentum through its own cut. An incident scalar profile by itself does none of those things. Density-gradient stress, conversion-layer storage, supports, moving walls and the ordinary scalar-field traction would need their own balance in the physical system. [Contact and density-stress limitations](../../software/em_charge_attribute/reports/rounded_end_bulk_flux.md#L17) · [Matched fixed-geometry example](../../software/em_charge_attribute/reports/joined_mouth_normal.md#L17)

# Independent receiver momentum check

The proposed sign and distance dependence follow for the specified upper receiver. Let \(J\) be the excess momentum supplied *to* the fluid across the entire inner cut, projected on the target-center tangent \(t=(e_x,\epsilon f_x(0))\). Use a steady, source-free fluid outside this cut, a slip wall and zero excess momentum flux at infinity in each bent state. The outward area vector on the lower wall is exactly \((\epsilon\nabla f,-1)d^3x\). Impermeability removes the advective current there. With \(p_\epsilon\) the wall pressure relative to the bath, momentum balance consequently gives

\[
J(\epsilon)=\epsilon\int_{r>a}p_\epsilon(x)[f_x(x)-f_x(0)]\,d^3x .
\]

The derivative requires continuity of the weighted pressure integral at zero bend. The unknown first pressure variation multiplies a vanishing zeroth-order projection. An \(O(\epsilon)\) change of the projected aperture edge likewise drops out for regular integrable pressure without concentrated rim forces. Unknown changes to the actual inner cut are already included in its conserved resultant. The supplier's reaction is \(-J\) when it owns that cut. This projection is the work per rigid center displacement along \(t\). A stationary intact wall has zero mechanical power. Rotating or deforming the supplier, or supporting the receiver separately, requires its additional work and momentum balances.

Take \(f(x)=\int q(y)/|x-y|\,d^3y\), absorbing the Green-function normalization in the nonnegative \(q\). For a point at \(y\), angularly averaging its gradient over a target-centered sphere gives \(y/|y|^3\) when \(r<|y|\) and zero when \(r>|y|\). A direct axial integration gives these two cases using the point-to-point distance as the integration variable. Consequently

\[
J'(0)=\int q(y)\frac{y_x}{|y|^3} C(|y|)\,d^3y,\qquad
C(s)=-4\pi\int_s^\infty p_0(r)r^2\,dr .
\]

For support in a ball of radius \(b\) centered at \(d e_x\), with \(d>a+b\), all axial weights are positive. Thus \(J'(0)/f_x(0)\) is a weighted mean between \(C(d+b)\) and \(C(d-b)\), regardless of the shape of \(q\) in that ball. For the point limit it equals \(C(d)\). The bent domain should first be linearized for a smooth finite source and then shrunk to the point source. For a finite half-space discharge with physical volume rate \(Q\) and density \(\rho\), the usual radial \(v\sim Q/(\pi^2r^3)\) and excess Bernoulli pressure give \(C(d)\sim 2\rho Q^2/(3\pi^3d^3)\). Multiplication by the incident \(d^{-2}\) slope gives a \(d^{-5}\) cut reaction away from the positive source. A uniform tilt gives zero exactly. This receiver omits the fluid flow from a second aperture and the actual feeding-side contact. It therefore excludes a \(d^{-2}\) contribution only in this cut response, for the stated geometry and common incident-height normalization.

guide_scope.md.verbatim_text:
# Mechanical audit of the widening guide

The proposed boundary conditions give a conditional example of like-orientation repulsion. They require separate ownership of the inlet preparation, guide, and downstream reaction. They also require a bulk direction that persists when the local brane turns.

For mass rate $D=\rho A_i v_i=\rho A_o v_o$, put $m=A_o/A_i>1$. At ambient outlet pressure the inlet excess pressure is $\rho(v_o^2-v_i^2)/2$. Including pressure on each cut gives $T_i=\rho A_i(v_i^2+v_o^2)/2$, $T_o=\rho A_i v_i v_o$ and $\Delta T=\rho A_i(v_i-v_o)^2/2>0$. Bernoulli conserves the total head through the guide. An upstream quiescent reservoir must supply the excess head $\rho v_o^2/2$ or receive the equivalent from a pump. The outgoing stream carries away $Dv_o^2/2$ and its directed momentum. Include ambient pressure on the outer guide when using excess pressures. For translating cut surfaces, pressure work includes $pA\,\mathbf U\cdot\mathbf n$ in addition to pressure times the through-flow.

For orientation $+$ let $Z=\ell\langle h\rangle_\eta$ and use a translating, force-only pivot receiving both port forces. Under translation or field variation, $\delta Z=\ell(\langle\delta h\rangle+\langle\nabla h\rangle\cdot\delta X)$. The same $\Delta T\,\delta Z$ supplies both the scalar source and its translation work. With the local spring included, this passive part gives $+L g$ for incident gradient $g$. The Cartesian input thrust adds $-\ell T_i u g$, yielding $B=L-\ell T_i u$ and $L=z\ell\Delta T$. At $k_m=0$, $u=z=1$ and $B=-\ell T_o$. Adding the vertical reaction again after evaluating scalar stress would duplicate the normal work. A finite guide transmitting an angle-dependent moment to the bend must also include the angular virtual work. Intersecting thrust axes at a torque-free ideal pivot are sufficient for the stipulated force-only joint.

The sign also follows for a regular, compact radial profile $\eta\ge0$ of unit integral, with the same sampling for height and inclination. Let $V=k_m\eta/\kappa\ge0$. A uniform incident offset has regular response $p(r)\to1$, with $(r^2p')'=r^2Vp$ and $z=\langle p\rangle_\eta$. Write the dipole solution as $h_1=gxv(r)$, $v\to1$, so $(r^4v')'=r^4Vv$. The maximum principle gives positive $p,v$ and these identities give $p',v'\ge0$. The radial operator $\partial_r^2+4\partial_r/r-V$ sends $p$ to $2p'/r\ge0$ and sends $v$ to zero, so $v\ge p$ by comparison. Angular averaging gives $u=\langle v+rv'/3\rangle_\eta\ge z>0$. The quantity inside the average has derivative $rVv/3\ge0$ and equals one outside the support. Thus $B\le-\ell zT_o<0$. For a uniform annulus $a<r<b$, $u=[b^3v(b)-a^3v(a)]/(b^3-a^3)$; the inner and outer edge values suffice. This argument assumes the dipole equation receives no angular actuator or support term.

For $k_m=0$ and a fixed widening ratio, universality requires $D^2/A_i$ constant. A sustained common pressure head with geometrically similar mouths instead gives constant velocities and thrusts proportional to area. Where $A_i\propto a^3$, the requisite $D\propto a^{3/2}$ entails excess upstream pressure head proportional to $a^{-3}$. For finite $k_m$, both $L$ and $B$ must be constant across physical radii for reciprocal, common-strength forces. Equalizing $L$ alone leaves $u/z$ in $B/L$.

**Counterexample to inferring the force from guide data.** Attach a lossless upstream elbow to the same translating mouth. Its two cuts have the inlet's pressure, area and speed. Its incident stream follows the bulk axis and its exit follows the tilted inlet. Its baseline normal thrust difference vanishes. Its lateral reaction $+\ell T_i u g$ cancels precisely the guide's Cartesian increment, leaving $B=L$. The guide itself still has the same mass rate, head, thrusts, bend source and outlet direction. If the elbow is separately supported, its reaction belongs to that support and the proposed negative $B$ survives. A joint can in principle transmit a pure torque without a net horizontal force, but a directional boundary condition alone does not specify that joint. Common rotation of both ports provides another check, giving zero tangent force for $k_m=0$. A separately supported feed and a downstream sink or return which does not reapply the reaction to the same body are substantive conditions for the example.

# Independent source and numerical fidelity check

**Verdict — Scoped clear for the three reports’ conditional force signs, power balances, radius comparisons, and receiver decay. The physical order-conversion mouth law remains unresolved.**

I checked the three reports against the Python and Wolfram sources, guard outcomes and literal output, including the warning-bearing runs. The synthesis correctly uses minus the holding-force change, the inward scalar delivery \(+sL\mathbf g\), and the outward force \(-s_ts_sB_tL_s/(4\pi\kappa d^2)\). The reciprocity and common-strength conditions assume one orientation-odd channel and nonzero emission on the branch. The historical 1.041412 emitter factor is rounded from 1.04141204803. The final text distinguishes a uniform height offset from an applied gradient, and specifies four independent orientation/gradient combinations.

For the guide, pressure-inclusive Bernoulli thrust gives \(T_i-T_o=\rho A_i(v_i-v_o)^2/2\). On a sharp sheet the horizontal inlet load is \(-s\ell T_i\mathbf g\) and the vertical work contributes \(+s\ell(T_i-T_o)\mathbf g\). Their sum is \(-s\ell T_o\mathbf g\). Attaching the upstream steering elbow restores \(B=L\); co-rotation gives zero sharp tangent response. The guide has zero power at rest and the signed moving-cut energy difference is its thrust work. On the annulus the scalar stress contributes \(sL\mathbf g\) and the independent horizontal inlet term samples the dipole slope gain \(u\). The fixed widening ratio fails reciprocity at the two tested radii. Both accepted calculations give \(B/L=-4.362378922,-4.185248474\), the emission-matching intake ratio 2.77162005175, and the small-target/large-target mixed-force ratio 1.04232256434 at \(m=2\). The stated pressure-head bounds follow for similar three-dimensional inlet cross-sections and nonnegative tension and curvature contributions. [Python guide output](../s11c/bend_flow_guide01/stdout) · [Accepted Wolfram series output](../s11c/bend_flow_guide_series_wolfram01/stdout)

For the half-space receiver, the wall momentum and inner injected momentum have the same sign; the supplier of the inner momentum receives the opposite reaction. The leading horizontal and vertical terms cancel within the target-center tangent projection. The reflected lower receiver changes sign for the same imposed height. The source-ball boundaries \(d-b,d+b\), point-limit formula, pressure tail and two force exponents match the independent source and screen integrals. All eight normalized values agree after rounding to the twelve decimals printed by Python. The Python integration warning concerns roundoff at the requested angular tolerance. The Wolfram finite-annulus NDSolve attempt produced integration failure and extrapolation messages on stdout despite a zero exit code. Its finite-annulus numerical values are discarded. The Wolfram series replacement completed cleanly and supplies the comparison quoted above. The free-mouth attachment, other receiver and feeding-side channels remain outside these benchmarks. [Discarded NDSolve output](../s11c/bend_flow_guide_wolfram01/stdout) · [Receiver warning](../s11c/curved_screen_receiver01/stderr) · [Independent receiver output](../s11c/curved_screen_receiver_wolfram01/stdout)

The manifest and review-comparison write-up are separate deliverables handled by the parent. I made no edits to the three reports and no commit.

**Addendum verdict — Scoped clear for the radius-dependent guide compatibility relations, including necessity, sufficiency and domain.** For the stated positive \(\ell,z,u,\rho,A_i,L_0\), finite widening \(m>1\) and inward mass rate \(D>0\), the baseline thrust identity gives \(L=\ell zD^2(1-1/m)^2/(2\rho A_i)\). """One-mouth stress and jet-direction checks for a weak applied bend."""
import sympy as sp

theta, b, epsilon, gradient, load, kappa = sp.symbols(
    "theta b epsilon g L kappa", positive=True
)
normal = sp.Matrix([sp.sin(theta), 0, sp.cos(theta)])
axis = sp.Matrix([0, 0, 1])
gradient_self = -load / (4 * sp.pi * kappa * b**2) * normal
gradient_total = gradient_self + epsilon * gradient * axis
flux = kappa * (
    gradient_total * gradient_total.T
    - sp.eye(3) * gradient_total.dot(gradient_total) / 2
)
outward_density = sp.trigsimp(axis.dot(flux * normal).diff(epsilon).subs(epsilon, 0))
outward = sp.simplify(sp.integrate(
    2 * sp.pi * b**2 * sp.sin(theta) * outward_density, (theta, 0, sp.pi)
))
print("outward axial cross traction per area:", outward_density)
print("total inward cross current:", -outward)
ell, thrust, s, cin, cout = sp.symbols("ell T s c_in c_out", real=True)

def beam(slope_response):
    vec = sp.Matrix([-slope_response * ell * epsilon * gradient, 1])
    return s * thrust * vec / sp.sqrt(vec.dot(vec))

jet_force = beam(cin) - beam(cout)
jet_susceptibility = sp.simplify(jet_force[0].diff(epsilon).subs(epsilon, 0) / gradient)
print("cartesian inlet minus outlet tilt susceptibility:", jet_susceptibility)
for inlet, outlet in [(0, 1), (1, 0), (1, 1)]:
    print("inlet,outlet", inlet, outlet, "susceptibility",
          jet_susceptibility.subs({cin: inlet, cout: outlet}))
tangent = sp.Matrix([1, ell * epsilon * gradient])
print("normal beam dotted with graph tangent:", sp.simplify(beam(1).dot(tangent)))
assert sp.simplify(-outward - load * gradient) == 0
assert sp.simplify(jet_susceptibility - s * thrust * ell * (cout - cin)) == 0
assert sp.simplify(beam(1).dot(tangent)) == 0

"""Direct angular integration of a displaced unit monopole on a receiver plane."""
import sympy as sp

r, d, distance, gap = sp.symbols("r d distance gap", positive=True)
u = sp.symbols("u", real=True)
# The change of variable is the physical point-to-point distance on the shell.
distance_squared = r**2 + d**2 - 2 * r * d * u
u_from_distance = sp.solve(distance_squared - distance**2, u)[0]
field_axial = (d - r * u) / distance_squared ** sp.Rational(3, 2)
shell_integrand = sp.simplify(
    -field_axial.subs(u, u_from_distance) * sp.diff(u_from_distance, distance) / 2
)
print("transformed shell integral density:", shell_integrand)
primitive = sp.integrate(shell_integrand, distance)
inside = (primitive.subs(distance, r + d) - primitive.subs(distance, d - r))
outside = (primitive.subs(distance, r + d) - primitive.subs(distance, r - d))
print("shell mean for r<d:", sp.factor(inside))
print("shell mean for r>d:", sp.factor(outside))
rho, discharge = sp.symbols("rho Q", positive=True)
speed = discharge / (sp.pi**2 * r**3)
tail = sp.integrate(4 * sp.pi * r**2 * rho * speed**2 / 2, (r, d, sp.oo))
print("leading pressure weight outside d:", tail)
assert sp.simplify(inside - d**-2) == 0
assert sp.simplify(outside) == 0

## Mathematical review (proof vs choice)

### 1. Scalar closed-surface stress (proof)

Take the bend energy
\[
E=\frac{\kappa}{2}\int|\nabla h|^2\,\mathrm{d}V,\qquad\kappa>0,
\]
so that away from the defect \(-\kappa\nabla^2 h=0\). The isolated stationary mouth of orientation \(s=\pm1\) and strength \(L(R)>0\) has the Coulomb tail
\[
h_{\mathrm{m}}=\frac{sL}{4\pi\kappa\,r}\qquad\Rightarrow\qquad -\kappa\nabla^2 h_{\mathrm{m}}=sL\,\delta^{(3)}.
\]
The associated Maxwell/Eshelby stress is
\[
T_{ij}=\kappa\Bigl(\partial_i h\,\partial_j h-\tfrac12\delta_{ij}|\nabla h|^2\Bigr).
\]
On any closed surface enclosing only this monopole, with outward normal (force on the enclosed defect), the linear response to a pure incident gradient \(\nabla h_{\mathrm{ext}}=g\) is exact:
\[
\mathbf{F}_{\mathrm{scalar}}=\oint\mathbf{T}\cdot\mathbf{n}\,\mathrm{d}A=-sL\,\mathbf{g}.
\]
(Equivalently: interaction energy \(U_{\mathrm{int}}=sL\,h_{\mathrm{ext}}(\mathbf{R})\), hence \(\mathbf{F}=-\nabla_{\mathbf{R}}U_{\mathrm{int}}\).)  
This is a theorem for the given quadratic functional and the given monopole. It does not depend on how \(L\) is maintained, nor on remote return of the legacy sink. Physical embedding height \(\ell h\) enters Newtonian bookkeeping only through virtual work on the tilted surface (below); it does not alter the \(h\)-stress integral itself.

### 2. Reciprocal, radius-independent repulsion (conditions)

Write the first-order mouth force under pure incident bend as \(\mathbf{F}= -s\,\Lambda\,\mathbf{g}+\mathbf{F}_{\mathrm{legacy}}^{(0)}\), where the legacy kernels are independent of \(g\) by assumption, so \(\mathbf{F}_{\mathrm{legacy}}^{(0)}\) drops out of the linear response.

**Necessary measurement conditions**
- Independent source: measure \(L\) (or the conserved constituent throughput that fixes \(L\)) without using force or displacement response.
- Signed response: measure \(\mathbf{F}/g\) for both \(s=+1\) and \(s=-1\) (or reverse \(\mathbf{g}\)) and verify oddness in \(s\).
- Reciprocity: the linear map \(g\mapsto F\) must equal the Maxwell partner (mouth displacement \(\mapsto\) bend moment / induced monopole response) at fixed constitutive state.
- Radius independence: repeat at more than one \(R\) on the same brane. Because \(F_{\mathrm{scalar}}\propto L(R)\), radius-independent repulsion requires either \(L\) independent of \(R\) or an additional \(R\)-dependent channel that cancels \(L(R)\) while preserving the sign \(-s\). Conserved constituent conversion alone does not cancel \(L(R)\).

Absent those four, “reciprocal radius-independent repulsion” is a physical claim, not a consequence of the scalar stress theorem.

### 3. Energy at a held mouth does not fix the force (proof)

Hold the mouth at the origin and vary uniform \(g\), taking the gauge \(h_{\mathrm{ext}}=g\cdot x\) so \(h_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)=0\). Then
\[
U_{\mathrm{int}}=sL\,h_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)=0
\]
for every \(g\). The cross term in field energy carries no information about \(\mathbf{F}=-sL g\). Force is the derivative with respect to mouth position, not with respect to \(g\) at fixed position. Therefore an energy-versus-uniform-bend curve at a held mouth cannot determine the scalar force. (IR-regularized bulk energy likewise fails: the cross term remains gauge-equivalent to zero for a pure gradient.)

### 4. Turning-stream momentum budget (choice + consistency checks)

Consider a reversible lossless stream of equal mass rate \(\dot m\) and equal speeds through two matched cuts. In a small bend along \(x\),
\[
\hat{\mathbf{u}}=\frac{(-b\,\ell\nabla h,\,1)}{|\cdots|}\approx(-b\,\ell\partial_x h,\,1)+O(|\nabla h|^2),
\]
with possibly distinct inlet/outlet factors \(b_{\mathrm{in}},b_{\mathrm{out}}\) and orientation \(s\). Keep receiver (bulk) reaction on a separate ledger.

**Horizontal momentum delivery from the cuts (to linear order)**
\[
\dot P_x=\dot m\,v\bigl(u_{\mathrm{in},x}-u_{\mathrm{out},x}\bigr)\approx\dot m\,v\,\ell\,g_x(b_{\mathrm{out}}-b_{\mathrm{in}})
\]
(up to the sign convention for flow sense and \(s\)). If the body rides the tilted surface, virtual work of the normal load \(N\) supplies an additional effective horizontal force \(N\cdot(\ell g)\) (ski-slope term).

**When unequal \(b\) is possible (physical choice, not proof)**  
Unequal \(b\) is allowed when the two cuts use different references: surface tangent (\(b=1\)), lab/world vertical (\(b=0\)), or a finite-patch average of \(\nabla h\) over a region of size \(\sim R\). It is not allowed if both cuts are required to use the same bulk asymptotic gauge. Common rotation of the whole apparatus produces no relative \(g\) and must be quotiented out; rigid world axes, local patch slopes, and genuine bulk \(\nabla h|_{\infty}\) are distinct observables.

**Does this evade \(\mathbf{F}_{\mathrm{scalar}}=-sL g\)?**  
No, not as an additional passive-scalar force. Evading would require either (i) double-counting, or (ii) an extra momentum channel outside \(E=\frac\kappa2\int|\nabla h|^2\).

### 5. Double-counting and neglected pressure (counterexamples)

- **Pressure on the cuts.** For a reversible lossless stream, Bernoulli fixes \(p+\frac12\rho v^2+\rho\,\ell h\) (or the appropriate enthalpy). Matched speeds do not imply matched pressures once heights or bend potentials differ. A pure \(\dot m\,\Delta\mathbf{u}\) account that omits face pressure is incomplete; the missing pressure force is first order in \(g\) and typically cancels part or all of the kinematic tilt term.
- **Normal load / virtual work.** If wall pressure (or \(N\)) is already included, adding the ski-slope virtual work again double-counts the same normal traction.
- **Scalar stress vs stream.** If the stream is the material realization of the order conversion that sources \(L\), its first-order horizontal delivery is not independent of \(\oint T\cdot n\); adding both overcounts. If the stream is an extra inertial channel, then \(\Lambda\) in §2 is no longer equal to \(L\), reciprocity with the pure scalar partner fails, and radius independence becomes a separate tuning of \(\dot m(R)\,v\,b\,\ell\) against \(L(R)\).
- **Legacy sink.** By hypothesis its source kernels do not depend on incident bend, so it contributes no \(O(g)\) piece; any \(O(g)\) stream claim must sit in the mouth/brane sector already constrained by the stress theorem.
- **Radius check is incomplete.** Matching \(F/g\) at two radii can hide: (i) couple stresses from finite-patch slope sampling, (ii) lip/contact-line forces with different \(R\) scaling that cancel in \(F\) but appear in torque, (iii) remote return of enthalpy/momentum (action on the separate receiving bulk), (iv) gauge confusion between common rotation and true bulk \(g\).

### 6. Sufficient measurements (operational)

1. Stress-integral or positional derivative of energy at fixed \(g\) (not energy vs \(g\) at fixed mouth) to obtain \(\mathbf{F}_{\mathrm{scalar}}\).  
2. Independent assay of \(L(R)\) and of \(\dot m,v\).  
3. Signed responses for both \(s\) and reversed \(g\).  
4. Explicit split of receiver-bulk reaction from body+brane.  
5. At least one check that replaces local patch slopes by a bulk asymptotic \(g\), and one that compares \(b_{\mathrm{in}}=b_{\mathrm{out}}\) (common reference) against deliberately unequal \(b\).  
6. Pressure-inclusive control-surface budget on the stream cuts; confirm that omitting pressure changes the inferred \(O(g)\) force.

### 7. Verdict

- **Proof:** closed-surface scalar stress contributes \(\mathbf{F}_{\mathrm{scalar}}=-sL\mathbf{g}\); held-mouth energy versus uniform bend does not determine this force; reciprocity and radius independence are extra conditions on independent source and signed response data.  
- **Physical choice:** stream tilt factors \(b\), inclusion/exclusion of cut pressure and ski-slope virtual work, and which slope reference (common rotation / world axes / patch / bulk) is used. None of these evade the passive scalar theorem without either double-counting normal load/pressure or introducing an extra channel that must be measured separately and that generally spoils radius-independent reciprocity.

---

### Runnable witness (local operator)

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Witness: monopole in uniform bend gradient — stress force vs held-mouth energy."""
import numpy as np

kappa, L, s = 1.0, 2.5, +1
g = np.array([0.3, 0.0, 0.0])  # incident bend gradient
R = 0.7                         # sphere radius for stress integral

def grad_h(x):
    r = np.linalg.norm(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
    # h = g·x + s L / (4 π κ r)
    gh_m = -s * L / (4 * np.pi * kappa) * x / r**3
    return g + gh_m.squeeze()

# Maxwell stress T_ij = κ (∂i h ∂j h - δij |∇h|^2 / 2)
# Force on defect: ∮ T · n dA, n outward from origin
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
n_fib = 80000
# Fibonacci-like sphere samples
u = rng.random(n_fib)
v = rng.random(n_fib)
th = np.arccos(2*u - 1)
ph = 2*np.pi*v
n = np.stack([np.sin(th)*np.cos(ph), np.sin(th)*np.sin(ph), np.cos(th)], axis=1)
x = R * n
dA = 4*np.pi*R**2 / n_fib
gh = np.array([grad_h(xi) for xi in x])
T_n = np.zeros(3)
for i in range(n_fib):
    gi, ni = gh[i], n[i]
    Tn = kappa * (gi * np.dot(gi, ni) - 0.5 * np.dot(gi, gi) * ni)
    T_n += Tn * dA

F_stress = T_n
F_theory = -s * L * g
U_held = s * L * 0.0   # h_ext(0)=0 in gauge h=g·x

print("F_stress ", F_stress)
print("F_theory ", F_theory)
print("rel err  ", np.linalg.norm(F_stress - F_theory) / np.linalg.norm(F_theory))
print("U_held(g)=", U_held, " (flat in g; does not encode force)")
assert np.linalg.norm(F_stress - F_theory) < 0.05 * np.linalg.norm(F_theory)
print("OK: stress = -s L g; held-mouth energy does not fix the force.")
```

Run: `python3 witness_bend_force.py`. Expected: relative error \(\lesssim\) few percent (Monte-Carlo), `U_held=0`, assertion passes.

source sign reconsideration.verbatim_text:
## Force on the body: \(+\int J\,\nabla h\)

With your Lagrangian and the given Green function, the force on the body is
\[
\mathbf{F}_{\text{on body}}=+\int J\,\nabla h\,dV
\]
(principal-value / “other” field). Like-signed positive sources attract. That overturns the opposite sign if an earlier pass chose \(-\int J\nabla h\).

---

### 1. Momentum density and spatial current (with source)

EOM from \(\mathcal{L}=\frac{M}{2}\dot h^2-\frac{\kappa}{2}|\nabla h|^2+Jh\):
\[
M\ddot h-\kappa\nabla^2 h=J.
\]
Static Green function matches the given self-field: \(h_{\text{self}}=+J_{\text{tot}}/(4\pi\kappa r)\).

Define the field momentum density so a right-moving packet carries positive momentum:
\[
p_i=-M\,\dot h\,\partial_i h.
\]
Multiplying the EOM by \(\partial_i h\) and rearranging yields the balance law
\[
\partial_t p_i+\partial_j\Sigma_{ji}=-J\,\partial_i h,
\]
with spatial momentum current (outside the support of \(J\), quasistatic piece shown)
\[
\Sigma_{ji}=\kappa\,(\partial_j h)(\partial_i h)+\delta_{ji}\Bigl(-\frac{M}{2}\dot h^2+\frac{\kappa}{2}|\nabla h|^2\Bigr).
\]
(The isotropic \(Jh\) contact piece sits only where \(J\neq0\); a surface lying entirely outside the body does not see it.)

RHS \(-J\partial_i h\) is the rate density at which momentum is fed into the field. Action–reaction on the source support therefore gives
\[
F_i^{\text{on body}}=+\int J\,\partial_i h\,dV.
\]

On-shell static energy \(\int\bigl(\frac{\kappa}{2}|\nabla h|^2-Jh\bigr)=-\frac12\int Jh\) makes the pair interaction
\[
E_{\text{int}}=-\sum_{a<b}\frac{Q_a Q_b}{4\pi\kappa\,r_{ab}}
\]
for monopole strengths \(Q=\int J\). Same-sign \(Q\) attract, and \(-\nabla_X E_{\text{int}}\) reproduces \(+\int J\nabla h_{\text{other}}\).

---

### 2. Reciprocal force from \(J(x-X)\) and virtual work

Interaction term \(\int J(x-X)\,h\,dV\). Varying the body coordinate at fixed field,
\[
\frac{\delta}{\delta X^i}\int J(x-X)\,h=+\int J\,\partial_i h
\]
(after one IBP). The generalized force conjugate to \(X\) is again \(+\int J\nabla h\).

Equivalently, take the potential for the body at fixed external field to be
\[
V(X)=-\int J(x-X)\,h_{\text{ext}}\,dV.
\]
Then \(F_i=-\partial V/\partial X^i=+\int J\partial_i h_{\text{ext}}\). Same sign, now read as virtual work including the interaction.

---

### 3. Surface integral = momentum delivered to the body

Integrate the balance law over a volume \(V\) that contains the body and whose boundary lies in the source-free region:
\[
\frac{d}{dt}P_i^{\text{field}}(V)+\oint_{\partial V}\Sigma_{ji}\,n_j\,dA=-\int_V J\,\partial_i h\,dV.
\]
Quasistatic translating body: field momentum inside \(V\) is steady, so
\[
F_i^{\text{on body}}=+\int J\partial_i h=-\oint\Sigma_{ji}\,n_j\,dA.
\]
The inward flux of field momentum through \(\partial V\) is exactly the force on the body. A numerical surface integral built from this \(\Sigma\) (with outward normal) equals \(-F\); the opposite orientation, or the continuum “force on contents” convention \(F_i=-\oint\Sigma_{ji}n_j\), equals \(+F\). Accepting the number while denying that it is momentum arrival at the body is a bookkeeping dispute about orientation/contact terms, not a second dynamical channel.

---

### 4. Signed source and receiver coefficients (\(a\) vs \(2a\))

For a single factorized massless scalar channel the ordered force is of the schematic form
\[
\mathbf{F}_{A\to B}=s_A\,r_B\,\nabla G(\mathbf{X}_B-\mathbf{X}_A),
\]
\[
\mathbf{F}_{B\to A}=s_B\,r_A\,\nabla G(\mathbf{X}_A-\mathbf{X}_B)=-s_B\,r_A\,\nabla G(\mathbf{X}_B-\mathbf{X}_A),
\]
with the same positive Green function that reproduces \(h_{\text{self}}=+Q/(4\pi\kappa r)\) when \(s=Q\).

Monopole bodies that both emit and respond through the same charge have
\[
s=r=Q=\int J
\]
(same sign for source and receiver). Radii \(a\) and \(2a\) may make \(|Q|\) scale differently with size (volume \(\sim a^3\), surface \(\sim a^2\), etc.); the signs stay the same for “positive” sources, and \(s=r\) still holds object by object.

---

### 5. Reciprocal equal nonzero strength in every ordered pairing

Demand Newton III and equal nonzero ordered strengths for every pair:
\[
s_A r_B=s_B r_A\neq0\qquad\text{for all pairs}.
\]
Already for three bodies this forces a single global ratio,
\[
\frac{s_i}{r_i}=\lambda\quad\text{(same \(\lambda\) for all bodies)}.
\]
A pure monopole channel realizes this with \(\lambda=1\), \(s_i=r_i=Q_i\). Independent source/receiver assignments that are not proportional (e.g. \(s\propto a\), \(r\propto a^3\) from mixed multipole bookkeeping) fail on some ordered pair and cannot be carried by one factorized massless scalar. Under the single-channel hypothesis the proposed “equal nonzero in every ordered pairing” condition therefore holds if and only if source and receiver coefficients stay proportional across bodies; same-type bodies of radii \(a\) and \(2a\) with \(s=r=Q\) pass.

---

### 6. Bernoulli / brane height

No. If the carrier action is only the quadratic scalar piece plus \(Jh\) and supplies no brane/Nambu–Goto or fluid constitutive term that identifies pressure with a height built from \(h\), Bernoulli does not force \(p=p(h)\). That relation is extra matter physics, not a consequence of the bulk scalar alone.

---

### 7. Concentric radial sampling of a harmonic incident gradient

No. In a source-free region \(\nabla^2 h=0\), so each Cartesian derivative \(\partial_i h\) is harmonic. Spherical means (and more generally concentric radial kernels) of a harmonic function equal its center value, independent of radius. Two concentric samplers of widths \(a\) and \(2a\) therefore read the same incident gradient; local radial sampling cannot by itself change it. (Scattering boundary conditions on real cavities can dress the total field; that is not pure incident sampling.)

---

### 8. Residual disagreement

The live dispute is not the surface algebra (agreed numerically) but its identification with momentum delivered to the body. With the continuity equation above, that identification holds in the quasistatic limit: inward \(\Sigma\)-flux \(=F_{\text{on body}}=+\int J\nabla h\). Opposite claims typically come from (i) flipping the outward-normal convention, (ii) dropping or double-counting the isotropic \(Jh\) contact stress inside the source, or (iii) importing electrostatic \(F=q\mathbf{E}=-q\nabla\phi\) without mirroring the sign built into \(h_{\text{self}}=+Q/(4\pi\kappa r)\) and \(\mathcal{H}=\cdots-Jh\).

Hidden-momentum / Abraham-style caveats matter for electromagnetic media with running fields; for this static real scalar with \(\dot h=0\) in the comoving frame they do not reverse the sign.

**Judgment retained:** force on the body is \(+\int J\nabla h\); the properly oriented surface integral of \(\Sigma\) is the momentum arrival rate at the translating body; same-sign monopoles attract; single-channel reciprocity constrains \(s_i/r_i\) to a common \(\lambda\); Bernoulli–\(h\) and width-dependent harmonic sampling are not forced by the stated action.

## Referee verdict

The throughflow construction is consistent as a **conditional** load-and-momentum model under the stated mouth bookkeeping, and the halfspace shell/tail identities check out. It does **not** supply a native throat law, a closed conservative particle energy, or a uniquely selected physical charge. Reciprocity with one common signed amplitude for all ordered radius pairs does **not** follow from any single widening ratio by choosing \(D(R)\). A rigid upstream elbow joined to the mouth changes the force/moment account.

**Agree** that the single stream is conditional; that cut thrust is \(Dv+(p-p_{\mathrm{amb}})A_{\mathrm{cut}}\) with equal total head and ambient outlet; that \(T_i-T_o=\frac{D^2}{\rho A}\frac{(m-1)^2}{2m^2}\ge 0\); that \(T_i-T_o=P\) with \(P=4\pi\sigma R^2+C\) is load balance, not throughput physics; that for \(k_m=0\) in the sharp idealization the draft’s \(B=-\ell T_o\) with \(L>0\) is the intended reduction; and that, in the quiescent halfspace problem, exterior/interior shell averages of \(\nabla f\), and the \(d^{-3}\) tail weight multiplying center slope \(d^{-2}\), are right.

### Five corrections

1. **Bath and virtual work.** With open steady \(\rho,D\neq 0\), pressure work and kinetic flux at the cuts exchange power with reservoirs. Particle-relevant virtual work on \(Z=\ell\langle h\rangle_\eta\), including the normal bend force and the lateral reaction on the translated annulus, is therefore not the variation of a closed state functional built only from \(\kappa\) and \(k_m\int\eta h^2/2\). Treating \(L\) and \(B\) as pure field-stored couplings hides that bath power; energy bookkeeping fails unless the pumps/reservoirs are put on the free-body diagram.

2. **Reciprocity and \(D(R)\).** For fixed \(m>1\), \(T_i/T_o=(m^2+1)/(2m)\) is independent of \(D\), and \(B/L\) in the \(k_m=0\) reduction tracks \(1/z(R)\), also independent of \(D\). The supplied pairs give required ratios \((1-z)/(u-z)\approx 1.214\) at radius 1 and \(\approx 1.207\) at radius 2, hence inconsistent widening ratios (\(m\approx 1.90\) vs \(m\approx 1.88\)). Choosing \(D(R)\) only rescales \(L\) and \(B\) together; it cannot enforce reciprocity plus one common signed amplitude for all ordered pairs at a single \(m\).

3. **Angular momentum and the elbow.** Inlet normal tied to the annulus-averaged sheet normal, with outlet on an independent bulk direction, produces a couple unless turning tractions are constrained by hand. Putting all guide turning on the mouth with “no net transmitted moment” is an assumption, not a consequence. A rigid upstream elbow joined to that mouth *does* change the result: it moves the steering force/moment off the declared mouth account and violates the “no silent upstream steering apparatus” clause.

4. **Support vs charge.** Matching \(T_i-T_o=P\) with one end transferred to the brane is a conditional axial load balance for the contact that carries \(Z=\ell\langle h\rangle_\eta\). The amplitude \(L=\ell z(T_i-T_o)\) is then a **conditional signed coupling**, fixed by \(m\), \(D(R)\), \(\ell\), and the load rule. The record does **not** select a physical charge; it selects a load-balanced throughflow amplitude open to falsification.

5. **Halfspace integral: sign, ownership, rate, boundaries.** Independently: after radial shell reduction, the surviving piece is \(\approx -f_x(0)\int_{r>d}p_0\,d^3x\); with \(p_0\sim -K/r^6\) and \(K>0\) this has the sign of \(\varepsilon f_x(0)\) times a positive tail weight, so the proposed INTO-receiver tangent quantity has that sign under the stated decay. It is a first-order **force** (rate of momentum transfer), not a momentum stock. The reaction on screen/inlet is opposite and must not be double-counted against graph pressure tractions. Needed hypotheses: otherwise impermeable static graph; quiescent exterior with vanishing excess momentum at infinity; \(p_0\) integrable near the bounded inlet with \(-K/r^6\) only as far decay (literal \(r^{-6}\) to the origin is not integrable in 3D); linearization in \(\varepsilon\); no other carrier injected.
